info.name: Exam Service
info.description:
Covers courses, exams, the full exam-attempt lifecycle (start -> answer -> finalize/grade -> cancel) and academic-record wiring for the Exam Service (see cpr/PAD-team1/exam-service/README.md section 8 for the auth/role table this mirrors).

Every request goes through the API Gateway (`base_url`, default http://localhost:8080): since 2.0.0 the service only accepts requests the Gateway forwarded, so calling it directly gives 401. This collection mints its own JWTs via the collection-level pre-request script (HS256 with `exp`, signed with the Gateway's secrets), and every run generates fresh, non-colliding course/exam/player ids, so importing it and clicking "Run" is enough — no manual token-pasting or id edits needed.

Folders 1-3 are safe to run automatically end-to-end. Folder 4 (the 410 expired-attempt case) is skipped automatically in a normal run — the attempt window is a real 10 minutes server-side, so it needs a manual wait; see its own description. The ExUnit suite already covers that case deterministically.

Before running, set the `jwt_secret` / `service_jwt_secret` collection variables to the `JWT_SECRET` / `SERVICE_JWT_SECRET` values from the team's `.env` (the ones the Gateway runs with), or pass them with newman's `--env-var`. The defaults are `change_me`, the placeholders in `.env.example`.

Temporary, until the Gateway is in the team's docker-compose.yaml: to call the service directly, set `base_url` to the service (http://localhost:4005) and `gateway_secret` to `GATEWAY_SECRET` from `.env`; the pre-request script then adds the identity headers the Gateway would send. Leave `gateway_secret` empty to go through the Gateway.

exec: // A run starts at the collection's first request (Create Course): it gets a fresh
// run_id and forgets the ids the previous run created, because the Postman app keeps
// collection variables between runs. Every later request reuses them, so two runs in a
// row never collide (no 422 on re-created data, no progress carried over).
// Minimal HS256 JWT signer using Postman's bundled CryptoJS — lets this collection
// mint its own valid player/moderator/service tokens instead of needing them pasted
// in by hand before every run.
// The Gateway verifies every token: HS256, signed with the Gateway's JWT_SECRET (player
// tokens) or SERVICE_JWT_SECRET (service tokens, sub "service:<name>"), and exp is required.
signJWT({ sub: pm.collectionVariables.get("player_id"), roles: ["player"], type: "player", iat: now, exp: now + 3600 }, jwtSecret)
signJWT({ sub: "postman-mod-" + runId, roles: ["player", "moderator"], type: "player", iat: now, exp: now + 3600 }, jwtSecret)
signJWT({ sub: "service:game-service", roles: ["service"], type: "service", iat: now, exp: now + 300 }, serviceSecret)
// TEMPORARY, until the Gateway is in docker-compose.yaml: with `gateway_secret` set (the
// GATEWAY_SECRET from .env) and `base_url` pointing straight at the service, send the
// headers the Gateway would add, built from this request's own token. Leave `gateway_secret`
// empty to go through the Gateway.

item.name: 4. Manual only — 410 expired attempt (skipped in a normal run)
item.description:
Skipped in a normal run: its request only runs once `expired_attempt_id` is set, so running the whole collection reports 0 failures. The attempt window is a real 10 minutes server-side (see ExamService.ExamAttempts @attempt_duration_seconds), so triggering a genuine 410 needs a real wait — there's no API to shorten it. The ExUnit suite covers this exact case deterministically (by inserting a pre-expired attempt directly into the DB), so this request exists purely for manual/exploratory testing.

To use it: run folder 1 once to get a course_id, start a fresh attempt via folder 2's "Start Attempt" request, copy its attempt_id into the `expired_attempt_id` collection variable, wait 10 minutes without finalizing it, then run this request.

request.description: Exam Service never names World Service in broker mode: it publishes `exam.passed`, and the broker delivers it to every subscriber. The wing's id comes from the course id (`zone-<course_id>-wing`).

exec: const done = (() => { try { return pm.response.code === 200 && pm.response.json().unlocked === true; } catch (e) { return false; } })();

pm.test("the Gateway gave the response a request id", () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("X-Request-Id")).to.be.a("string").and.not.empty);
